item.content:encoded:
…packs of children who appeared identical.

This detail really jumps out at me for some reason. Wonder what they wished for and got X-tuplets instead? A barren couple wishing for a child could be pretty common, and standard Wishmaster interpretation means "He" would do the fathering. But I can't see enough ladies falling for that after the first time for the offspring to count as a pack.
Maybe just one well-meaning juggler asked for the tribe to be fertile and multiply, giving us a Village Of The Damned situation. That would also account for the kids being abandoned en masse to turn feral and pack up.
Or maybe it was a horndog guy who wished for virility and/or to be irresistible to the ladies. And all those kids just look identical because they take after their father, who can't even begin to support all the bastards he's fathered.

Anything that gets my speculation gears turning gets an upvote. Bonus points for having a built-in reason why this tribe doesn't rule the world with their genie on demand; a day and a half of juggling is not something just anyone can pull off on a whim.

Yeah, I totally missed this when it was originally posted, I guess that is a good thing because it was obviously much improved…

For me the best part is that this is some sort of wish fulfillment or good luck item that is difficult to use, and when it finally worked the Foundation had absolutely no idea what to ask for or do with it. It's like they were taken by surprise when it worked, or just lacked the cultural understanding that the original crafters had in order to get a good harvest or any other kind of boon from this thing.
